new_defects.title: Thirty-five items score zero under a rule the repair itself created (W7 unexecuted)
new_defects.detail: SCORING.md section 1.2, as amended for W7, requires every item's ## Scoring section to carry a fixed native->ladder row and states that an item with no ladder row is unmeasurable and scores 0, fail-closed. Measured today: 6 of 137 items carry the mandated row verbatim (all six in 12-weapons); 102 of 137 carry a band table that does the job in a different format and are substantively but not formally compliant; 35 of 137 carry no native->ladder mapping in any form and therefore score 0 as written. The 35 include all six 86-ui items (among them RI-UIX02, the enforcement point for AR-2/S8), four of five 87-audio items, five of eight 40-dialogue items (including RI-DLG01 and RI-DLG05), five of seven 60-lore items, seven of nine 30-quests items including RI-QST06 (the main quest), six of nine 70-visual, plus RI-AI01 and RI-MTH01. Three of the fourteen wave-1 pieces in docs/PLAN.md are therefore unscoreable on day one. CORPUS-COHERENCE-01 section 12.2 flagged this honestly at the time; 73 items were then written while the rule was live and only the six weapons items complied, because the rule is invisible to corpus-index.mjs --check.
new_defects.fix: One pass by area owners filling the row for the 35; either reconcile the other 96 to the mandated format or amend SCORING.md section 1.2 to accept any table mapping a native band to a ladder number. Add the row's presence to corpus-index.mjs --check as C6.

new_defects.title: The corpus grew 114% and nobody re-summed it; still no aggregate content budget
new_defects.detail: Gate G7's fifth clause. The enemy budget was reconciled properly (576 -> derivation-N and floor, census 1230, normalisation rule preserving RI-PRG06's soul column). That was one axis; nobody did the others, and 73 new items added new counts. Summing what the corpus currently demands: ~117,000 words of settlement-local dialogue (RI-DLG02 tier targets against settlements.json's 1 capital, 2 cities, 3 towns, 2 villages, 16 minor); a global reachable pool of ~80-90,000 words to satisfy the 0.28 locality ratio; 112 book texts at median 520 words (~65,000 words); 24-28 quests per faction line; >=5.5xN side quests (~80); a main quest at Morrowind's depth; 269 named NPCs; 250 interiors; 1,230 hand-placed enemies over 14.5 km2; 180 placed strangeness instances (30 elements x >=6); 55 spell effects; 15 weapon classes with full movesets; 9 birthsigns and >=6 origins; 15 working sanctioned breakages; 41 demonstrated seam crossings; >=15 opacity register entries and >=5 void tracts. That is an authored surface at or above Morrowind's base game, for a browser game, and no item, report or plan states the total or argues it is reachable. The failure mode an unreachable aggregate produces is not duplication (which a dozen items check for) but UNIFORM THINNING - every count met, every count met at its floor - and no instrument in the corpus fires when everything is simultaneously at the minimum.
new_defects.fix: corpus/00-doctrine/CONTENT-BUDGET.md: one table summing every count threshold into totals for words, quests, NPCs, interiors, enemies, placed instances and unique assets; each total with a named owning item; one signed paragraph stating whether the total is producible in the planned waves and what is cut first if not.

new_defects.title: The wave plan did not grow with the corpus
new_defects.detail: docs/PLAN.md's wave-1 decomposition is unchanged: fourteen pieces, written against a 200-path taxonomy. There is no builder for camera, character creation, weapon movesets, magic, stealth, crime, UI, audio or platform. Against that: RI-EXP01 is a DEAD-capable item whose binding beat sheet requires character creation, >=7 exercised verbs including sneak, and a hub with >=3 unfenced exits; RI-QST05's PACIFIST-ALL is now unmeasurable => 0 without RI-STL01/02 and RI-CRM01, so the W6 fix makes wave 1 fail the quest dimension by construction if stealth and crime are unbuilt; RI-CMP01's crossing floor cannot be met by fourteen pieces that exclude most of the crossing systems; and S25 makes the S18 third-person camera load-bearing for the water model rather than a deferrable presentation choice. This is an orchestration consequence rather than a corpus defect, but it will present in wave 1 as a run of hard fails on items whose prerequisites were never assigned.
new_defects.fix: Re-derive the wave-1 piece list against all 323 paths and assign every path a wave, so 'not built yet' is a declared state rather than a scoring-time surprise.

new_defects.title: RI-VIS03 still carries four bands its own reference population fails; M9 is the answer to 'does any new bar fail its own reference game'
new_defects.detail: tools/metrics/image-metrics.mjs now implements all twelve metrics with a self-test proving the instrument can fail - real progress from two. But METRICS-IMPLEMENTATION-01 section 8 states the position: M1 and M8 are calibrated; M2, M4, M5 are close; M3, M6, M9 and M10 have bands the reference population fails; M11 and M12 have never been run on real data at all. With the necessary highlight_frac gate already applied, 17 of 24 real Witcher 3 next-gen frames still hard-fail M9.ShoulderRatio < 0.12 -> LINEAR CLAMP, and not one is a linear clamp. M10.R_aerial's band 0.25-0.70 is failed at p10, p50 and p90 by the same population. The report proposes the corrections with evidence attached in exactly the form RI-VIS03's own step 7 demands, and RI-VIS03 has not adopted them - a grep for ShoulderRatio, advisory or an amendment block returns only the original band table. Compounding it: the modern fidelity set holds one usable HUD-free frame against RI-VIS03's own requirement of >=3 legally-usable frames per profile across four profiles, and the only populated profile is HUD-bearing and barred from numeric comparison by the acquisition request's section 5a. critic.fidelity cannot issue an admissible verdict today and nothing in the corpus says so. Note the report's own withdrawals W1 and W2 show why this must not be rushed: both were band amendments computed from a broken statistic, and adopting either would have hard-coded an instrument bug into the corpus.
new_defects.fix: Adopt METRICS-IMPLEMENTATION-01 section 7.1's A1-A3 and section 7.2's two withdrawals into RI-VIS03 now; mark M3, M6, M9, M10 advisory-not-scoring until the modern set lands; record in RI-VIS02 that fidelity verdicts are unmeasurable => 0 for any profile with fewer than three legally-usable frames.

new_defects.title: --check is asserted to be a blocking CI gate and is wired to nothing
new_defects.detail: RI-MTH05 M8 states '--check is wired as a blocking gate. It must run on any change to...', and its failure mode 4 is '--check made non-blocking, or the gate removed from CI'. There is no .github/, no package.json and no git hook in the repository. Nothing invokes it. The tool itself is sound and exits nonzero correctly, but a gate nobody runs is the same false-enforcement pattern W5 identified - it tells a reader the check is happening when it is not. This is the mechanism that let 147 orphaned paths and three doubly-owned constants survive an entire wave while INDEX.md reported 'up to date'.
new_defects.fix: A pre-commit hook or a two-line CI job running node tools/corpus-index.mjs --check. Until it exists, RI-MTH05 M8 should read 'must be wired', not 'is wired'.

hollowness_assessment.question: Would a game that scored well on all 137 items be Morrowind's world, quests, dialogue, factions, journal, lore and strangeness with Dark Souls' combat, in Black Marsh - or could it pass everything and be hollow?
hollowness_assessment.answer: It would be the thing that was asked for. The reason is not the 73 extra items but one mechanism: PLAYTHROUGH-CRITIC.md section 4.5's sabotage control. Every number in the experience battery is meaningless in isolation - nobody knows what detour_rate = 2.1/h should be - so the corpus only ever interprets the battery as a difference from a control: the same commit run twice, once through a sabotage filter, the critic blind to which is which, and VOID rather than FAIL if the instrument cannot separate them at the stated margin. That converts 'can an agent tell whether a game is any good' from a philosophical objection into a per-wave experiment with a recorded answer.

residual_routes_to_hollowness.detail: PLAYTHROUGH-CRITIC section 10 names this as the most likely single failure: the control is the most expensive thing in the corpus and the least obviously necessary, and once it stops running the numbers become decoration and the area reverts to the travelogue section 4.8 bans. There is currently no mechanical enforcement - it depends entirely on the orchestrator producing sabotage variants each wave. The verdict extension has a sabotage_control object but nothing rejects a verdict that omits it.

Section 4.7 is honest: audio, impact, tactile feel, input latency, frame rate, physical comfort, beauty, frustration, fatigue and attachment over weeks are outside the instrument and score unmeasurable => 0 fail-closed, which is the right rule and does not make them measured. Section 4.7 then says the true thing - 'the ultimate instrument for those properties is a human playing the game, and this corpus should say so' - and the corpus does not yet say so anywhere binding. There is no item, doctrine clause or wave gate requiring that a human ever play this before it is called done. PLAYTHROUGH-CRITIC builds exactly the right packs for it (worst-twenty-minutes clips, blind first hours, the two endings, the sabotage pair) and nothing requires anyone to look at them. This is the last real hole in the bar and it cannot be closed by commissioning another reference item.
